g11-history-uh6-t1.overview: Medieval African States sits inside Africa and the Outside World: 1500-1880s. Slave trade dominates Unit 6 of Grade 11 History, aligned to the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, the medieval African states of Funj, Morocco, Benin, Oyo, and the Zulu. Then the early contacts between Africa and Portugal along the coasts. Next, slavery inside Africa and the Atlantic, Indian Ocean, and Red Sea slave trade. Also the legitimate trade in palm oil and other goods after abolition. Finally, white settlement in South Africa and the European explorers and missionaries. Students will also learn how the slave trade shaped Africa and the wider world in later times.
objectives: Explain the rise and fall of the medieval African states.
Describe how the triangular trade worked.
Analyse the impact of enslavement on Africa and its people.
Discuss the shift to legitimate trade after abolition.
Trace the growth of white settlement in South Africa.
g11-history-uh6-t1.simple:
Medieval African States in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the Funj Sultanate, Morocco, Benin, Oyo, Ashante, and the Zulu kingdom.
  • Also the Kongo, Mutapa, and Rozwi states of central and southern Africa.
g11-history-uh6-t1.detailed:
Medieval African States — the essentials. First, the Funj Sultanate, Morocco, Benin, Oyo, Ashante, and the Zulu kingdom. Also the Kongo, Mutapa, and Rozwi states of central and southern Africa.

  • Explain the rise and fall of the medieval African states.
  • Describe how the triangular trade worked.
  • Analyse the impact of enslavement on Africa and its people.
  • Discuss the shift to legitimate trade after abolition.
  • Trace the growth of white settlement in South Africa.
